title: Word Nerds
blurb: Odd origins, secret meanings and the language trivia nobody asked for.

prompts.text: The word 'pandemonium' was invented by the poet John _____ for the capital of Hell in Paradise Lost.
Lewis Carroll invented the word 'chortle' by blending 'chuckle' and _____.
Alexander Graham Bell wanted people to answer the telephone by saying '_____', but 'hello' won out.
The word 'mortgage' comes from Old French for 'death _____'.
The coffee 'cappuccino' is named after the brown robes of _____ friars.
The word 'vaccine' comes from the Latin word for _____.
The word 'pedigree' comes from French for 'crane's _____', after a branching mark in old family trees.
The word 'calculate' comes from the Latin for a small _____ once used for counting.
The word 'sarcasm' comes from a Greek word meaning 'to tear _____'.
The word 'window' comes from Old Norse words meaning 'wind _____'.
The word 'candidate' comes from the Latin for 'dressed in _____', the colour of a Roman office-seeker's toga.
The flower name 'dandelion' comes from French for 'lion's _____'.
The language with the most native speakers in the world is _____.
The country with the most languages, over 800, is _____.
Only one letter of the alphabet does not appear in any US state name: _____.
The dot over a lowercase 'i' has its own name: the _____.
Besides hash and pound, the # symbol is sometimes known as the _____.
In Italian, the @ symbol is called a chiocciola, which means _____.
The punctuation mark that combines a question mark and an exclamation mark is called the _____.
The constructed language Esperanto was created in 1887 by the eye doctor L. L. _____.
The Klingon language from Star Trek was developed by the linguist Marc _____.
J.R.R. Tolkien invented two main Elvish languages: Sindarin and _____.
Louis Braille, inventor of the reading system for the blind, lost his own sight as a child in an accident with his father's _____.
In Cockney rhyming slang, 'apples and pears' means _____.
In Aussie slang, a 'servo' is a _____.
In Australian English, a 'doona' is a _____.
The world's longest official place name, as listed by Guinness World Records, belongs to a hill in _____.
The Welsh village with the longest place name in the United Kingdom, Llanfairpwllgwyngyll and so on, is on the island of _____.
Most Icelanders use patronymics instead of family _____.
Written Japanese mixes kanji, hiragana and a third script called _____.
The Korean alphabet, Hangul, was designed in the 1440s under King _____.
The French scholar who cracked Egyptian hieroglyphs in 1822 was Jean-Francois _____.
Samuel Johnson published his Dictionary of the English Language in the year _____.
Dr William Minor sent thousands of quotations to the Oxford English Dictionary while living in a criminal _____.
'Floccinaucinihilipilification' is the act of deciding something is _____.
A word that spells a different word backwards, like 'stressed' and 'desserts', is called a _____.
'Eunoia', the shortest English word containing all five vowels, means 'beautiful _____'.
Misusing a word in a silly way is called a malapropism, named after a character in Sheridan's play The _____.
The word 'whisky' comes from the Gaelic 'uisge beatha', meaning water of _____.
The Japanese word 'karaoke' means 'empty _____'.
The word 'safari' is Swahili for _____.
The word 'orangutan' is Malay for 'person of the _____'.
The word 'bungalow' comes from an Indian word for a house in the style of the region of _____.
The word 'khaki' came into English via Hindi and Urdu from a Persian word meaning _____.
The word 'dinosaur' was coined in 1842 by the English palaeontologist Richard _____.
